newsitem.title: UK: EU working week ruling will cost UK business - CBI.
newsitem.headline: EU working week ruling will cost UK business - CBI.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry (CBI) said on Tuesday that the European Court ruling on working hours "will add to some of industries' costs".
But CBI director general Adair Turner told Reuters that considerable flexibility in interpreting the directive, and "loopholes" means it is possible to negate some of its impact.
"Given all this flexibility it is possible to negate much of the impact on business," he said.
Turner called on the government to consult industry on how the directive would be implemented, and to offer "clear guidance."
On Tuesday the European Court of Justice rejected the main part of Britain's challenge to an EU law on working hours and rest periods.
In a statement, the CBI attacked the directive as "legislation at its worst - detailed and prescriptive regulations followed by extensive caveats and exemptions."
The CBI said it is urging the government "to make full use of the exemptions available in the directive given that the effect of the directive will depend on how it is implemented."
The employers' organisation said the government could introduce legislation allowing the 48-hour maximum working week to be averaged over up to 12 months. -- Jonathan Birt +44 171 542 7715
